title: Unequal Power Was Not Unequal Worth
definition: An arrangement in which some groups have more power or privileges than others.
content:
Colonial society included unequal power and privileges. A privilege is an advantage given to particular people or groups. Historical records could use categories connected with ancestry, birthplace, office or tax status. These categories were made and used within a system of rule. They were not a measure of intelligence, character or human worth.

In this mission, we examine what a label did in a particular record. Did it affect a payment, an office or access to an opportunity? Do not treat every category as one fixed ladder applying unchanged to all people throughout Spanish rule. A person could have several roles, and social relationships could change. Our fictional record cards are tools for asking questions, not a game of assigning classmates to ranks. Students will not disclose ancestry or receive points for belonging to a group.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit this lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Power
A hierarchy concerns unequal power and privileges within a system.
Historical labels
Ask how a category was used in its dated setting.
Equal worth
Colonial categories do not determine any persons human worth.
task: A colonial category is presented as a measure of a persons worth. What correction fits?
Explain how the label affected power or treatment without ranking human worth
Use the category to rank classmates
Treat the category as a measure of intelligence
Assume every person had an identical role
reason: Explain how the label affected power or treatment without ranking human worth. Colonial categories do not determine any persons human worth.

title: An Office and a Person Were Different
definition: A term used for a local elite associated with municipal offices and their families, with meaning depending on context.
content:
Local elites could connect colonial authorities with community affairs. Majuls discussion describes the principalia in relation to town offices and families. Knowing that a person held office helps identify a role, but not every action that person took. A title does not prove fair conduct, universal approval or identical behavior by all officeholders.

Compare fictional cards for an instruction, an officeholder and a complaint. The instruction concerns an official task. The name identifies a person in a role. The complaint records a reported problem. Connect them only when their people, place and period match. Do not assume that local leaders always agreed with every colonial demand or that every official had the same resources. A local role could involve carrying out instructions and raising difficulties; each action needs its own evidence.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit this lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: A local role
Principalia relates to local elite roles and families in colonial municipal society.
Title and action
An office title alone does not establish how its holder acted.
Context
Check place, period and particular responsibilities before generalizing.
task: An office title is used as proof that an official always acted fairly. What should be checked?
Evidence of the persons actual actions in that setting
Nothing because titles guarantee fairness
Whether every family had that office
A classmates ancestry
reason: Evidence of the persons actual actions in that setting. Check place, period and particular responsibilities before generalizing.

title: Labels Could Shape Treatment
definition: A classification used in rules or records about taxation.
content:
Colonial labels could affect treatment in matters such as taxation and local authority. Aguilars study of Gregorio Sancianco explains a critique of tribute as a source of divisions among people. This connects a revenue system with social relationships. A category in a record is therefore something to investigate, not a neutral description of every part of a persons life.

Use a fictional tax register with two category headings but no rates supplied. The headings show that the writer distinguished groups. They do not let us invent exact payment amounts or conclude that every member had the same wealth, work or opportunities. To explain an actual difference, find the dated rule and the relevant entry. We may discuss the historical term mestizo when a source uses it, but it does not automatically mean wealthy, official or one identical background in every record.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit this lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Rules and categories
A classification could matter to how colonial rules treated people.
Named critique
Sancianco criticized tribute for contributing to social divisions.
No automatic biography
A category alone does not establish wealth, occupation or every experience.
task: A tax-category label is used to invent a persons exact income. What should change?
Use evidence for income and distinguish it from the classification
Treat every member as equally wealthy
Use the category to decide human worth
Assume every member held office
reason: Use evidence for income and distinguish it from the classification. A category alone does not establish wealth, occupation or every experience.

title: Compare Opportunities in Everyday Life
definition: A practical chance to take part in an activity or pursue a goal.
content:
Unequal resources and power could shape everyday opportunities. Access to schooling, time for work, control of resources and connections with officials are questions to investigate. A category alone cannot tell us exactly how every household experienced them. Records about an institution or a prominent person may leave other people less visible.

Compare two fictional learner cards without ancestry labels. One has time, materials and a nearby class; the other lacks those supports. The model shows why an available opportunity on paper is not necessarily equally reachable. It is not a historical census or a claim about every child in one group. Ask what support and constraints each card describes. We do not ask students to disclose family income or judge classmates. For a historical report, replace assumptions with dated evidence about particular people and circumstances.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit this lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Practical access
An opportunity depends on the conditions that let someone take part.
Compare conditions
Time, materials and location can matter alongside an institutional rule.
Model limit
Fictional learner cards do not establish every historical households experience.
task: Two fictional learners face different practical supports. What does the model illustrate?
An opportunity can be differently reachable under different conditions
Ancestry determines intelligence
Every child had identical access
The cards are a complete historical census
reason: An opportunity can be differently reachable under different conditions. Fictional learner cards do not establish every historical households experience.

title: A Named Case: A Petition from Bacolor
definition: A formal request made to an authority.
content:
A UP Diliman research summary describes Chinese mestizo chiefs in Bacolor, Pampanga, petitioning colonial authorities in 1698 for relief from tribute-collection duties. The case connects a social category with a local role and a request. It shows why a label alone is too small to explain a persons place in community life.

The study discusses an investigation and local relationships, including recognition by native elites. This is a particular historical case, not a rule that every petition succeeded or every person in the category held land. Separate the request, the investigation and any documented result. Our labelled clue card is a modern source guide, not a surviving petition page. We do not invent speeches, signatures or personal motives. Explain what people requested and what evidence the study provides, while leaving wider claims open to further investigation.

Open the three clues and choose an explanation they support. Use Explain for help or revisit this lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Place and period
The named petition concerns Bacolor, Pampanga, in 1698.
Role and action
Chiefs made a request concerning tribute-collection duties.
Scope
A petition, an investigation and a final outcome are distinct evidence questions.
task: What does the Bacolor example help show?
A named category, local role and petition need to be understood together
Every person in the category held identical land
Every petition automatically succeeded
A label supplies every private motive
reason: A named category, local role and petition need to be understood together. A petition, an investigation and a final outcome are distinct evidence questions.

title: Prepare Your Everyday Experience Report
definition: A formal request made to an authority.
content: Review five ideas. Hierarchies involved unequal power and privilege, not unequal human worth. An office identified a role rather than every action. Categories could affect treatment without explaining a whole life. Practical conditions shaped opportunities. The Bacolor petition is a named case connecting categories, roles and a recorded request. Prepare a fictional report for another Grade 5 learner. Name the people or role, place and period. Give a supporting clue and identify what you cannot yet know. Do not turn a category into guaranteed wealth, intelligence or behavior. Label learner cards as fictional models, and separate a petition from its documented outcome. You do not need to disclose ancestry, religion or family finances. The main quiz has five questions and three correct passes. If needed, return to linked learning content before practice and a retry. Completing this mission earns its configured reward once, but does not complete Chapter 10. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.

The named petition concerns Bacolor, Pampanga, in 1698.
Role and action
Chiefs made a request concerning tribute-collection duties.
Scope
A petition, an investigation and a final outcome are distinct evidence questions.
task: Which report best explains colonial social experience?
Connect categories, roles and conditions with dated evidence without ranking human worth
Use ancestry as a measure of intelligence
Assume a title guarantees fair conduct
Treat one petition as every persons story
reason: Explain unequal power and varied experiences through evidence, while recognizing every persons equal human worth.
